Edda.narrative: I keep the berry rows alive, the pots full, and my store dry; a winter does not care whether a planter has had a good year. I sell to both towns because neither can eat pride, and trade days are what carry my household through the cold. I have buried my husband and will not let my children mistake stubbornness for strength.
goals: Keep the berry fields productive and the seed store sound.
Earn enough from trade days to see the household through winter.
Keep Colm from turning his anger into a quarrel that costs us trade.
Edda.mood: Practical, watchful, and a little worried about the coming winter.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a good heart, but it runs ahead of his sense when he is angry.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She wanders farther than I like, but she notices what others miss.

relations.name: Kari
relations.label: niece
relations.note: My sister's girl knows how to keep a store without wasting a crumb.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She has kept the stone's peace longer than most could manage.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She does sound work and asks little of anyone.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He tends his planting honestly, even when the hunters make a mess of it.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: A healer's hands are worth more than gossip about whom she married.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He counts every berry, but he pays and keeps the market moving.

memories.gist: The first winter after my husband died, I kept the seed jars beside the hearth and counted what we could spare before I let the children see how little was left.
Last spring, Colm and I repaired the low stone edging after frost pushed it out of place; he worked until his hands blistered and never once complained.
At a trade day, I sold a full basket of berries to Dunstan and came home with salt and smoked fish enough to make the next week easier.
I found fresh damage in the berry bushes where hunters had cut across the rows, and had to pull Briar away before she went looking for them herself.

stances.why: The stores last longer when both towns bring what the other lacks.
Oathstone earns its place by giving both sides somewhere to meet without choosing a side.
A trampled bush takes seasons to recover, not one angry afternoon.
Being right about a wrong does not make every response wise.

Colm.narrative: I know what it takes to coax food from the ground and what it feels like to watch careless boots undo it. I want the Keeper's work because the stone needs someone who will hear a grievance plainly and make people answer for it. I can keep my temper—until someone treats our fields as if they belong to nobody.
goals: Be recognized as a serious choice to succeed Aud as Keeper of the Stone.
Protect the berry fields from hunters crossing them carelessly.
Earn Elin's affection without making her feel caught between towns.
Colm.mood: Earnest and impatient, with anger close to the surface.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She sees the cost of every choice before I do, and usually tells me so.

relations.name: Briar
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She can vanish into the fields all day and still come back knowing more than I do.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: I respect what she has done, but she will not tell me whether she thinks I can do it.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: courtship
relations.note: I care for her, and I wish the towns made that simpler.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has skill enough to help at the stone, if she would stop refusing every responsibility.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He knows what it is to have his land crossed by hunters who think only of the chase.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His hunters have no right to trample our bushes and call it their need.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He follows Brann across our fields as if the Oath and our work mean nothing.

memories.gist: I found the berry bushes crushed where Brann's hunters had crossed the rows. I was so angry I had to walk away before I said something I could not take back.
Mother showed me how to brace the stone edging against spring runoff, and made me redo the section I had rushed.
The last midsummer renewal, I stood near the ring and watched Aud hear the words that keep the towns from turning every grievance into bloodshed.
Elin and I spoke after a trade day, when the market noise had thinned. I remember how easy it was to talk until I thought about what our families might say.

stances.why: The village cannot remain a meeting ground if people treat its fields as empty land.
A grievance ignored grows into a feud; it should be heard before it turns into one.
Both towns need passage and trade, even when one side has acted badly.
The Keeper serves the stone, not one town or one household.

Briar.narrative: I like the quiet places where reeds bend over the water and the berry leaves hide the sky. Mother worries when I walk far, and Colm worries louder, but I come back with useful things and usually a story. Some things I see belong to the people I saw, not to everyone who might ask.
goals: Gather good reeds and find useful plants without being hurried home.
Keep peace with Colm even when he wants me to take his side in every quarrel.
Hold on to the small, private things people trust me not to repeat.
Briar.mood: Dreamy and observant, with a guarded streak.

relations.name: Edda
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She understands why I bring home odd plants, even when she pretends to scold me.

relations.name: Colm
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is easier to love when he is not trying to make the whole village agree with him.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She listens without rushing to fill a silence.

relations.name: Elin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is practical, but she has a gentler way of hearing people than she lets on.

relations.name: Runa
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: I have seen her among the trees, and I think she likes the quiet as much as I do.

relations.name: Wenna
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She has a bright, restless look, like she is always on her way somewhere.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: He knows the planted ground and does not laugh at my questions about it.

memories.gist: I went down to the lake for reeds and saw Runa and Wenna together by the water. They seemed to want the moment to themselves, so I kept walking and have not told anyone.
Mother taught me to sort the good reeds from the brittle ones, then showed me how to weave a basket that would not sag under berries.
Colm came looking for me after I walked farther than I meant to. He was cross, but he carried my reeds back without making me ask.

stances.why: Seeing something does not make it mine to turn into village talk.
Plants and reeds take time to grow back, even when people are in a hurry.
Quiet gives me room to notice what a crowd would miss.

Briar.secret: I saw Runa and Wenna together by the lake and suspect their meetings are private for a reason. I have told no one.
